$comment: Phase 06 (Workspace Engine) resolved against repository artefacts: architecture/phase-06-workspace-engine.md (now with addendum IE), frontend/src/lib/kernel/phase-contracts/phase-06-workspace-engine.ts, registry row 06, and the workspace modules.

documentIntegrity.finding: The document stated 18 of the 20 mandatory engineering sections; the memory and knowledge sections were absent. Addendum section IE (Workspace Memory and Knowledge) was authored in the document's own lettered style, stating what a workspace remembers (session state, context history, preferences, saved/shared views, recent activity, snapshots) and what it knows (navigation catalog, module registry, composition contracts, component registry, capability contract, status/dependency health) — with the rules that keep memory authorization-bound and knowledge projected rather than copied.

ownership.note: Phase 06 composes and presents; it never owns identity (02), tenancy (03), educational reality (04), execution (05), authorization (08/09) or reasoning (26).

areas.area: Workspace concept, types, hierarchy and identity (F–I)
areas.requirement: A workspace is a typed, tenant-scoped composition with a stable identity and an optional hierarchy — never a page.

areas.area: Workspace lifecycle: creation, activation, suspension, archiving, deletion (J–O)
areas.requirement: A workspace has a managed lifecycle with defined states rather than an implicit existence.

areas.area: Membership, membership states and workspace roles (P/Q/S/U)
areas.requirement: Access to a workspace is expressed as membership with a role and a state, ranked and validated.
Navigation is composed from contributions and withheld unless the viewer's capabilities allow it.
Modules are registered per workspace with an explicit enabled/disabled/deprecated status.

areas.area: Pages, dashboards, cards and widget contracts (AE–AS)
areas.requirement: Surfaces are composed from versioned contracts, so a widget type has a lifecycle and a version rather than ad-hoc markup.

areas.area: Preferences, saved/shared views, filters, sorting, grouping (AZ–BJ)
areas.requirement: A view (filters, sort, grouping, ownership, sharing) is a first-class object, not a UI session detail.

areas.area: Workspace context, session state, snapshots and versioning (BX–CE)
areas.requirement: Workspace configuration is versioned and snapshot-able so a change can be reviewed and rolled back.

areas.area: Template ownership, versioning, inheritance and overrides (CG–CK)
areas.requirement: Templates inherit with explicit, validated override rules instead of silent divergence.

areas.area: Workspace policy, governance, administration and audit boundary (CM–CQ)
areas.requirement: Workspace configuration is policy-validated, administrable and auditable; the engine does not own the audit trail.

areas.area: RBAC, ReBAC, classification, widget security and sandboxing (DN–DZ)
areas.requirement: Visibility and action availability follow authorization from Phase 08/09; sensitive widgets are classified and sandboxed.
Composition respects accessibility, locale and branding rules rather than assuming one language or one theme.

areas.area: Role-optimised experience, empty workspace and help (HO–HS)
areas.requirement: Each role receives the workspace its authority implies; an unauthorized workspace resolves to empty rather than to a default page.

areas.area: Data residency, region-aware workspaces and currency display (HV–HZ)
areas.requirement: Regional placement and currency presentation follow the tenant's configuration rather than a global default.
Workspace lifecycle changes are expressed as typed events owned by the engine.
areas.boundaryNote: The event vocabulary exists in the workspace contract, but nothing emits it: no server function records a workspace lifecycle event. Declared, not enforced — registered as owned debt (06).

areas.area: Workspace provisioning, export, cloning, reset and snapshot restore (GZ–HG)
areas.requirement: Workspaces can be provisioned idempotently, exported, cloned, reset and restored from a snapshot.
areas.boundaryNote: Only snapshotting/versioning exists; there is no workspace export, clone, reset or restore path, and no idempotent provisioning contract. Reserved: needs a persistence substrate for workspaces, which phase 06 deliberately does not own. Registered as owned debt (06).

areas.area: Workspace composition projected in a surface, catalog-driven (L4)
areas.requirement: The composition a viewer receives is inspectable from real engine output, and the full role catalog is accounted for without any hand-written role list.
areas.boundaryNote: The `/super-admin/workspace-projection` L4 surface was removed with the hardcoded console UI (2026-10-26). The neutral engine and Scholar adapter remain; projection is IMPLEMENTED_UNWIRED until a governed replacement surface exists.

areas.area: Engineering-section completeness of the phase document
areas.requirement: The document states the mandatory engineering sections, including what a workspace remembers and knows.
